title: Intermediate-Mass Black Holes in Dense Clusters and Dwarf Nuclei: Dynamical, Accretion and Gravitational-Wave Budgets Against Density and Energy Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Tariq Rahal, and this is Intermediate-Mass Black Holes in Dense Clusters and Dwarf Nuclei: Dynamical, Accretion and Gravitational-Wave Budgets Against Density and Energy Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Tariq Rahal, and this is Intermediate-Mass Black Holes in Dense Clusters and Dwarf Nuclei: Dynamical, Accretion and Gravitational-Wave Budgets Against Density and Energy Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'47 Tucanae: Pulsar Timing, Velocity Dispersion and the Central Mass Budget'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): central_mass_solar = 2300; sphere_of_influence_pc = 0.06869728374305084; eddington_luminosity_erg_s = 2.898e+41; eddington_ratio = 1.725327812284334e-10; bondi_rate_solar_per_yr = 1.155706730726586e-05; fundamental_plane_radio_erg_s = 2.352500447408869e+28.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'HLX-1 in ESO 243-49: Outburst Luminosity, State Transitions and the Mass Scale'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): central_mass_solar = 20000; sphere_of_influence_pc = 0.03440837863999764; eddington_luminosity_erg_s = 2.52e+42; eddington_ratio = 3.9682539682539684; bondi_rate_solar_per_yr = 0.0008738803256911802; fundamental_plane_radio_erg_s = 7.67014186489349e+35.
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Henize 2-10: A Compact Radio Nucleus in a Dwarf Starburst and Its Mass Caveat'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): central_mass_solar = 1000000; sphere_of_influence_pc = 2.6881545812498153; eddington_luminosity_erg_s = 1.26e+44; eddington_ratio = 7.936507936507937e-05; bondi_rate_solar_per_yr = 2.18470081422795; fundamental_plane_radio_erg_s = 2.5703957827688435e+35.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Intermediate-Mass Black Hole Mergers: Chirp Mass, Strain and the LISA Detection Budget'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): central_mass_solar = 2000; sphere_of_influence_pc = 0.021505236649998524; eddington_luminosity_erg_s = 2.52e+41; eddington_ratio = 3.968253968253968e-08; bondi_rate_solar_per_yr = 8.738803256911803e-06; fundamental_plane_radio_erg_s = 5.067612475423897e+29; chirp_mass_solar = 870.5505632961239.
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'M15: Central Mass Concentration, Pulsar Accelerations and the Compact-Object Budget'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): central_mass_solar = 1700; sphere_of_influence_pc = 0.037305002352038256; eddington_luminosity_erg_s = 2.142e+41; eddington_ratio = 4.6685340802987856e-08; bondi_rate_solar_per_yr = 6.313785353118777e-06; fundamental_plane_radio_erg_s = 4.4642669750777184e+29.
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'M62: Central Mass Concentration and the Radio and X-Ray Accretion Test'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): central_mass_solar = 3000; sphere_of_influence_pc = 0.0573472977333294; eddington_luminosity_erg_s = 3.78e+41; eddington_ratio = 5.2910052910052905e-08; bondi_rate_solar_per_yr = 1.9662307328051553e-05; fundamental_plane_radio_erg_s = 1.0538348976044637e+30.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “47 Tucanae: Pulsar Timing, Velocity Dispersion and the Central Mass Budget”. Its stated result is: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): central_mass_solar = 2300; sphere_of_influence_pc = 0.06869728374305084; eddington_luminosity_erg_s = 2.898e+41; eddington_ratio = 1.725327812284334e-10; bondi_rate_solar_per_yr = 1.155706730726586e-05; fundamental_plane_radio_erg_s = 2.3525004474 (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; '47 Tucanae: Pulsar Timing, Velocity Dispersion and the Central Mass Budget'; 'HLX-1 in ESO 243-49: Outburst Luminosity, State Transitions and the Mass Scale'; 'Henize 2-10: A Compact Radio Nucleus in a Dwarf Starburst and Its Mass Caveat'; 'Intermediate-Mass Black Hole Mergers: Chirp Mass, Strain and the LISA Detection Budget'; 'M15: Central Mass Concentration, Pulsar Accelerations and the Compact-Object Budget'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.
